n: One of the most personal psalms. David marvels that the Lord has searched him through and through and knows him completely.
God knows when he sits down and when he gets up, and understands his thoughts from far away.

f.w: thou understandest my thought afar off

n: God sifts through his travels and his rest, and is familiar with all his habits.
Before a word even reaches his tongue, God already knows it completely.
God surrounds him behind and in front, resting his hand on him — both protection and loving closeness.
Such knowledge is too wonderful and lofty for him to grasp.
Where could he go to escape God’s Spirit or presence? Nowhere — and that is a comfort, not a threat.

f.w: Whither shall I go from thy spirit?

n: Whether he rises to heaven or lies down in Sheol, the world of the dead, God is there.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol, the grave or world of the dead.

n: Even if he flew on the wings of dawn to the farthest sea in the west…

f.g: Swift as the light of sunrise spreading across the sky.

n: …God’s hand would still guide and hold him.

f.w: thy right hand shall hold me

n: If he hoped darkness would hide him, the night itself would become light around him.

f.w: Surely the darkness shall cover me

n: Darkness hides nothing from God; to him night shines like day.

f.w: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee

n: God formed his innermost being and knit him together in his mother’s womb.

f.g: Kidneys — the inner self, the seat of emotions.

f.w: covered me in my mother's womb

n: He praises God for making him in an awe-inspiring, wonderful way. God’s works are marvelous, and he knows it deep within.
His frame was not hidden from God when he was being formed in secret, skillfully woven as if in the depths of the earth — a poetic picture of the womb.

f.w: the lowest parts of the earth
f.g: A poetic image for the hidden place of formation.

n: God saw him as an unformed embryo, and every one of his days was written in God’s book before any of them began. Latter-day Saints also see in God’s foreknowledge our premortal existence.
God’s thoughts toward him are precious and vast.

f.w: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me

n: They outnumber the grains of sand. When he wakes, God is still with him.

f.w: more in number than the sand
when I awake, I am still with thee

n: The tone shifts sharply. David asks God to end the violent wicked and tells bloodthirsty men to leave him.

f.g: Men guilty of bloodshed; violent people.

n: They speak of God with malice and misuse his name.
He asks rhetorically: don’t I hate those who hate you, Lord, and loathe those who rebel against you?

f.g: Do I not loathe or feel disgust?

n: He hates them with complete hatred, counting God’s enemies as his own. This voices total loyalty to God; the New Testament later teaches us to hate evil while loving and praying for enemies.

f.w: I hate them with perfect hatred

n: Then a humble turn: rather than only judging others, he asks God to search him too. ‘Try me’ means test me as metal is tested; ‘thoughts’ means anxious thoughts.

f.g: Test me, as metal is tested.

n: ‘See if there is any hurtful way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.’ The psalm ends in a prayer for guidance toward eternal life.

f.g: Any path of pain or idolatry.
